definition.text: A conventional collection-name for early Christian writings such as First Clement, the letters of Ignatius, and Polycarp’s letter. The collection title is not a claim that every work was written by an apostle.
definition.locator: ANF1 volume title and named works
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: The Teaching of the Twelve Apostles: an anonymous early Christian text presenting the two ways, initiation, thanksgiving, community order, and watchfulness.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: The Didache’s contrast between the way of life and the way of death, followed by concrete teaching about conduct.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Irenaeus’s account of Christ gathering up and renewing human life in himself, undoing disobedience through his obedience and uniting humanity to God.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: The systems opposed by Irenaeus that claimed superior, hidden knowledge and distinguished their teaching from the public apostolic proclamation. The title covers varied opponents, not one identical system.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: The received confession or teaching of Christian faith used in patristic argument; in Irenaeus’s account the apostolic proclamation is public and preserved in the churches.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: A name Justin uses for baptism, connecting the washing with the understanding received by those learning these things.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: New birth; Justin describes baptismal washing in relation to being born again through Christ and receiving remission of sins.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: A defense or reasoned presentation of Christian faith, as in Justin’s address to the imperial authorities. Here the word does not mean an admission of fault.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: A letter, such as Clement’s letter to the Corinthians or Polycarp’s letter to the Philippians. The literary label itself does not establish scriptural status.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Receiving and caring for others; the Didache discusses welcoming travelers while also testing claims and avoiding exploitation.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: One who speaks a message from God. Justin appeals to the ancient prophets as witnesses to Christ; the Didache also discusses prophets within Christian communities.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: The anointed one; Cyril relates the name Christ to anointing while explaining the names Jesus and Christ.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Becoming God’s children by grace; Cyril distinguishes the Father’s relation to his Only-begotten Son from the adoption given to believers.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: A maker or craftsman; in the systems Irenaeus opposes, the term appears in a separation of the maker of the world from higher divine realities. Irenaeus argues for the one Creator.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Fullness; in the opposing systems described by Irenaeus, a name for a supposed higher divine realm. Its sense there must be distinguished from Christian uses of fullness.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Pertaining to Valentinus or the teachings criticized under that name in Irenaeus’s Against Heresies. The label identifies the historical opponent in that work.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: The claim that Christ’s humanity or suffering was only an appearance. Irenaeus defends the reality of the Incarnation and Christ’s saving human life.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Accounting or reckoning to someone; Westminster uses the term in its account of justification, distinguishing imputed righteousness from righteousness infused into the believer.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Westminster’s term for God’s calling of those predestined to life through his Word and Spirit, including renewal of the will and an effectual drawing to Christ.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: In Westminster’s teaching, those accepted in Christ, effectually called, and sanctified cannot totally or finally fall from grace. This is a specific confessional claim, not simply a synonym for endurance.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Westminster’s designation for the whole number of the elect gathered under Christ. Its definition is distinct from its account of the visible church.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Westminster’s designation for those throughout the world who profess the true religion, together with their children. Read alongside its separate account of the invisible church.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Westminster’s phrase for the relation between the sign and the thing signified in a sacrament, allowing their names and effects to be attributed to one another.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Church rites treated as neither commanded nor forbidden in God’s Word. The Formula of Concord discusses their use, Christian liberty, and limits in times of persecution.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Disordered desire; the Augsburg Confession includes it in its description of the inherited condition of sin. Read this term within that confession’s account rather than assuming identical usage in every tradition.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: The Augsburg Confession’s title for its teaching that faith should bring forth good fruits and commanded good works, while denying that works merit justification.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: Right belief; Philaret calls the Church Orthodox or rightly-believing in connection with the apostolic doctrine and succession.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: The five books of Moses: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.

definition.text: The union of divinity and humanity in the one person or hypostasis of Christ, without dividing him into two persons or confusing his two natures.
definition.reason: Necessary concise definition of terminology encountered in the linked published reading.
